advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the stamp rule should reverse-check against the EFFECTIVE (per-project) reverse of status_map rather than the built-in jira_to_local_status, to avoid over-stamping injective custom remaps.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_labels.py:105: forward = config.local_to_jira_status if status_map is None else status_map

Docstring claims: 'a label is needed IFF the local status has a Jira target AND that target does NOT reverse-map ... back to the local status — i.e. the forward mapping is lossy' but a per-project remap to a custom name is not reverse-mappable via the BUILT-IN map even when the per-project mapping is injective/lossless.
advisory.finding: _desired_status_annotation always reverse-checks against the BUILT-IN config.jira_to_local_status, even when a per-project status_map remaps a status to a CUSTOM Jira name absent from the built-in reverse map. For an injective (lossless) per-project remap such as in_progress -> "Doing", the built-in reverse lookup returns None (!= in_progress), so a rebar-status:in_progress label is stamped despite the mapping being perfectly round-trippable from the workflow status alone. This contradicts the documented "stamp IFF the forward mapping is lossy" intent and pollutes Jira labels for configs that only rename statuses.
scenarios: Operator config remaps a single status to a custom-but-injective Jira name (e.g. [mapping.projects.REB.status_map] in_progress = "Doing")

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the drift-warning dedupe should be keyed by (project_key, status) rather than status alone to avoid cross-project suppression.
evidence: Dedupe key is the bare status name `value`; multi-project passes share one process-global set so a per-project drift can be masked by an unrelated project's earlier warning for the same status name.
advisory.finding: The drift-warning dedupe set _DRIFT_WARNED is process-global and keyed by local status name ONLY (not by project). In a multi-project reconcile pass a status that drifts (no target) under project A's map will be suppressed for project B under a different map, and vice-versa, so a genuinely-drifting status in one project can be silently swallowed after the same status name was already warned for another project.
scenarios: A reconcile pass syncing tickets across multiple projects with differing effective status maps where the same local status name is mappable in one project and drifted in another

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an autouse fixture that calls outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings() before each test so the process-global _DRIFT_WARNED set cannot leak between tests.
evidence: outbound_mapper.py:44 `_DRIFT_WARNED: set[str] = set()` — module-level per-process state
outbound_mapper.py:62 `if value not in _DRIFT_WARNED:` — a status warns at most once per process
test_status_mapping.py:145-146 `warn = capsys.readouterr().err` / `assert "blocked" in warn` — passes only if 'blocked' has not previously been warned in the session
search_files: `reset_drift_warnings` appears only at test_status_mapping.py:376 (the dedup test), so no autouse fixture clears _DRIFT_WARNED between tests

test_drift_warning_deduped_within_pass warns 'blocked' (resolve_outbound_status("blocked", {"open": "To Do"})) and does not reset afterward, so a reordering that runs it before test_unmapped_status_drifts would leave 'blocked' primed and break the earlier assertion
advisory.finding: resolve_outbound_status emits its drift warning via a process-global mutable set (_DRIFT_WARNED) that is never reset by an autouse fixture; only test_drift_warning_deduped_within_pass resets it (at its start, not end). test_unmapped_status_drifts asserts 'blocked' produces a stderr warning but depends on 'blocked' not already being present in the global set, making the test order-dependent and vulnerable to cross-test state pollution.
scenarios: Any future/parallel test in the session that drifts 'blocked' before test_status_mapping.py runs
Test reordering (e.g. pytest-randomly) placing the dedup test before test_unmapped_status_drifts
advisory.suggested_fix:
Add `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _reset_drift(): from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import outbound_mapper; outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings(); yield` (or call it at the top of each drift-asserting test) so drift-warning assertions do not depend on global session state.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Memoize `effective_status_map` per (project_key, repo_root) so the per-ticket outbound loop resolves each project's status map once instead of re-walking config discovery for every ticket.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:423 `for ticket in local_tickets:` drives the loop; each iteration reaches `_effective_status_map_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)` (create path outbound_differ.py:443-444 / update path outbound_differ.py:468-469).
config.py:95-100 `effective_status_map` calls `mc.load_mapping_config(root)` unconditionally per call; mapping_config.py:213-215 calls `_config.read_reserved_section('mapping', root)`.

rebar/config.py:616 `read_reserved_section` calls `_discover_project_config(root)`, which walks directories upward doing `rt.is_file()` / `pp.is_file()` / `.git` `exists()` syscalls per level (_config_sources.py:191-206) on every call.

The raw TOML parse IS cached by (path,mtime,size) via `_TOML_CACHE` (_config_sources.py:141-150), so the cost per ticket is the stat-walk + `_parse_layer`/`resolve_for_project` dict-merge work, not a file re-parse — but that work still scales linearly with ticket count.
No cache keyed by (project_key, repo_root) exists between `_effective_status_map_for` and `effective_status_map`; resolve_for_project rebuilds merged axis dicts each call (mapping_config.py:274-285).
advisory.finding: `_effective_status_map_for` recomputes the effective status map per ticket inside the `compute_outbound_mutations` loop, redoing config discovery (a filesystem stat-walk in `_discover_project_config`) and the three-layer resolution once per ticket with no memoization keyed by (project_key, repo_root), even though the result is identical for all tickets sharing a project key.
scenarios: A reconcile pass over a store with many local tickets (data volume scales with the project) repeats the config-discovery stat-walk and status-map resolution once per ticket, most of which share the same project key and thus resolve to the identical map.
advisory.suggested_fix: Cache the resolved map keyed by (project_key, repo_root) — e.g. a dict built once per `compute_outbound_mutations` call and consulted inside `_effective_status_map_for`, or an `functools.lru_cache`-style memo on `config.effective_status_map` invalidated per pass — so tickets sharing a project key reuse a single resolution and the config-discovery stat-walk runs once, not once per ticket.
